attempts.reason_tested: already published: canine babesiosis severity data exist
attempts.method: grep for kynurenin|tryptophan|indoleamine|IDO1|quinolin in /core/articles/CB*.md (0 hits) and /core/data/markdown/CB*.md (CB071, CB091); read both contexts; checked CB137 (saliva metabolomics, same group) for the same terms. PubMed query (dog OR dogs OR canine) AND (babesia OR babesiosis) AND (kynurenine OR tryptophan OR indoleamine OR metabolomics), 2026-11-12.
attempts.result: PubMed returned 3 records, all from the Zagreb group and all in the CB set: CB091 serum metabolomics (10.3390/ijms23031575), CB071 urine metabolomics by kidney function (10.3389/fmicb.2021.715701) and CB137 saliva metabolomics (10.3390/biom15040520, no kynurenine or tryptophan term in the text). CB091 reports kynurenine higher in 12 B. canis-infected dogs than in 12 healthy dogs, with no severity or outcome contrast. No canine babesiosis study relates the kynurenine pathway to severity or outcome.

attempts.reason_tested: a severity-proxy contrast already exists in the published supplements
attempts.method: Re-analysed the published supplementary tables held read-only in /core/data/raw (script /experiments/SV-META/refutation/scripts/K09_kynurenine_supplements.py, seed 20261112): CB091 Table S2A (Biocrates p400 serum, 12 infected vs 12 controls) for Kyn, Trp and Kyn/Trp; CB071 Table 2A (urine targeted) for Trp and Table 1A (urine untargeted) for the three features annotated as kynurenine, across the control group and the kidney-function groups A (non-azotaemic, UPC < 0.5), B (non-azotaemic, UPC > 0.5) and C (azotaemic).
attempts.result: CB091 serum confirms the infection contrast and strengthens it: kynurenine median 17.9 vs 5.43 (Cliff's delta +0.97, Mann-Whitney p 6.0e-05) and Kyn/Trp 0.180 vs 0.055 (delta +0.86, p 3.8e-04), with tryptophan not different (delta +0.26, p 0.29). This is infected versus healthy, so it is not a severity result. CB071 urine gives the nearest thing to a severity contrast, by renal dysfunction: targeted tryptophan did not differ across groups A, B and C (Kruskal-Wallis p 0.31; C versus A delta +0.07, p 0.93), and none of the three untargeted kynurenine-annotated features differed across A, B and C (Kruskal-Wallis p 0.49, 0.95, 0.67). So a weak severity-proxy null already exists, in urine, in B. canis, with 5 to 10 dogs per group. It does not close the gap (urine is not plasma, renal function is only a proxy, annotation is untargeted and the groups are tiny) but it is evidence against a large effect in mild B. canis disease.

attempts.reason_tested: human severity evidence weak or unverified
attempts.method: Resolved the grid DOIs in PubMed: 10.1371/journal.pone.0087538 and 10.1186/s12936-017-1954-1 resolve; 10.1086/650996 and 10.3349/ymj.2022.0324 returned no PubMed record in this pass and are unverified here. Searched for further cohorts: 10.1515/cclm-2016-0912, 10.1038/srep20391, 10.1186/s40635-022-00445-8, 10.1007/s11306-024-02089-z.
attempts.result: Strong and replicated in sepsis and critical illness. Kynurenine was one of 7 metabolites in a network predicting 28-day ICU mortality, with replication in a second cohort (90 and 149 patients; 10.1371/journal.pone.0087538). IDO activity (kynurenine:tryptophan) and low tryptophan independently predicted death or ICU admission in 268 pneumonia patients, adjusted OR 9.1 (10.1515/cclm-2016-0912). Kynurenine was associated with 90-day survival in septic shock (10.1038/srep20391) and was among the 13 metabolites most strongly linked to sepsis mortality by ensemble machine learning (10.1186/s40635-022-00445-8); kynurenate was raised and tryptophan the one metabolite lowered in septic shock (10.1007/s11306-024-02089-z). In cerebral malaria, CSF kynurenine and kynurenic acid tracked coma duration and later cognitive impairment in 69 Ugandan children (10.1186/s12936-017-1954-1). Several independent cohorts, consistent direction; grade 3 holds.

attempts.reason_tested: mechanism may not transfer to Babesia, or is confounded
attempts.method: Reasoning from the human abstracts above and the CB071 renal groups; no new data.
attempts.result: Two caveats, neither fatal. The malaria evidence is largely CSF and cerebral (coma duration, cognition), and cerebral involvement is uncommon in B. rossi, so the brain pathway transfers poorly; the systemic sepsis evidence, which does not depend on cytoadherence, is the part that transfers. Second, kynurenine accumulates with reduced renal clearance and rises with any interferon-driven inflammation, so in babesiosis it will be confounded by azotaemia (a component of the complicated label) and by overall inflammatory intensity; CB091 itself links kynurenine to endothelial dysfunction via thrombomodulin, which is already measured in dogs. A canine study must adjust for creatinine and CRP. The vasodilatory action of kynurenine is a plausible fit for B. rossi hypotension, but that is an inference.

A validated LC-MS/MS method quantifies serotonin, kynurenine and tryptophan in canine plasma (limits of quantification 0.35, 0.22 and 4.2 ng/mL, intra- and inter-day precision under 15%; 10.1177/10406387261447261), and IDO activity and kynurenic acid have been used in dogs with pyometra (10.1016/j.theriogenology.2015.01.009). The Biocrates p400 kit used by CB091 also reports kynurenine in dog serum. Assay condition met.

attempts.reason_tested: testable with existing data, and double counting
attempts.method: Checked /core/data/raw for the two supplement archives, the sample lists in CB091 Table S4 and the CB071 group counts, the cohort fields of the CB071, CB091 and CB137 notes, and the SV-07 source list in the brief.
attempts.result: Existing files give per-dog kynurenine and tryptophan for 12 infected and 12 control dogs (CB091 serum) and urine values for 22 infected dogs in three renal groups (CB071), but neither file carries a severity grade or an outcome, so no true severity test is possible now. CB071, CB091 and CB137 are all cohort CH06 (Zagreb, B. canis, same ethics approval), so their dogs may overlap and must not be counted as independent sources. DS07 contains no kynurenine pathway protein and the pathway is metabolite, not protein; DS06 holds IDO1 and KMO RNA in 5 Beagles with no severity contrast. A real test needs stored serum or plasma with a hard outcome, which means the Onderstepoort B. rossi material.

verdict_reason: No canine babesiosis study has measured the kynurenine pathway against severity or outcome; CB091 is an infected-versus-healthy contrast, which my re-analysis of its supplement confirms is large (Kyn/Trp delta +0.86, p 3.8e-04). The human sepsis and critical-illness evidence is strong across several cohorts and a validated canine plasma LC-MS/MS assay exists, so tier D holds. It is weakened because the nearest severity proxy that can be computed now, the CB071 renal-function groups, shows no urinary kynurenine or tryptophan difference, because the malaria evidence is mostly CSF and cerebral, and because kynurenine is confounded by azotaemia and by inflammatory intensity.
